why: Python, one dominant maintainer, and a release rhythm of routine maintenance: `update dev dependencies` episodes that re-emit the CI workflow templates and a 1 000-line lockfile are the single most common thing the top decile of the risk score produced, which is the pattern this guardrail exists to catch or to refuse to catch. Its `test_weakening` cases are real too: test coverage genuinely deleted and genuinely rewritten in place, episodes apart.
pinned_by: looprs (agent, reco-dyt, 2026-10-20): re-pinned to widen the window from 60 episodes to 180 — the miss-rate gate's denominator was 7 and a 0.20 gate on 7 samples cannot tell 0.20 from 0.60, so the corpus grew rather than the bar moving. head is the branch tip at the time of the re-pin (unchanged since e4.9: flask had not moved), the window is the 180 newest episodes above it, and `python3 tools/fetch_g3_corpus.py` fetches the pin at depth `window * 4 + 20`. The previous pass was e4.9 (`reco-mkl.1`, 2026-10-19) at the same tip. `pinned_now` is a fixed instant above every commit date in the window, because the harness's clock is a field and never a read.
